answer: Give every identity a living ember: a behavioural relic that only forms from months of distinct activity — timing, choices, and the strangers it serves. Each epoch the network measures pairwise correlation between identities; a plume of look-alike profiles sharing one operator's rhythm is folded into a single vote. A lone agent keeps its ember glowing cheaply, but a farm running a hundred clones must fake a hundred genuinely different lives, each with its own timing and tastes — cost that grows per clone and cannot be pooled, because copying a life is exactly what the check detects.
